name: Carnegie Mellon University Cloud Lab (with Emerald Cloud Lab)
brief: A remotely operated university lab with more than 100 types of instruments for life sciences and chemistry, run primarily by robots and technicians, able to run more than 100 complex experiments at once.

cost.original: $26 million to acquire the lab's instruments (part of a $40 million project), 2021-2023
cost.excludes_note: Instruments only. The wider $40M project adds facility infrastructure and construction (about $14M implied). Software, staff and operating costs not included.

notes: Kept unverified: the US$26M instruments figure comes from one secondary source (universitybusiness.com); CMU's own release gives only the $40M project total. Verified 3 Oct 2026. University Business (trade magazine, opened via curl): "It cost CMU $26 million to acquire the lab's instruments". C&EN (Sep 2021, opened) gives only "The $40 million facility" and Tradeline returns HTTP 403 (not opened), so $26M rests on one secondary source; CMU's own release gives the $40M project including construction. Compare predictions against $26M for the instruments-only like-for-like, $40M for the whole project. No catalog mapping: the instrument list is not itemised publicly.
